text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) with potential subungual involvement.

Given your significant smoking history, African origin, and non-healing lesions on both the penis and finger, these findings are highly suspicious for SCC rather than syphilis or eczema. We have already ordered a biopsy and dermoscopy; please await the results to confirm the malignancy and determine the extent of the disease.
